name: Django
summary: A batteries-included Python web framework that composes configured applications, URL resolution, middleware, views, templates, and an object-relational model around a request/response lifecycle.
scope: ORM model registry and query boundary

features.name: Configured application registry
features.description: Django populates an Apps registry from installed application entries, creates AppConfig objects, imports application and model modules, and tracks application configurations and registered models.
benefits: Centralizes application discovery and model readiness
Supports reusable applications with explicit configuration boundaries
costs: Initialization order and readiness states constrain import-time behavior
Global registry state requires careful test and process isolation

features.name: URL resolver and view dispatch
features.description: URLResolver recursively matches URL patterns, captures positional or keyword arguments, and returns a ResolverMatch that identifies the callback and route metadata for view dispatch.
benefits: Separates URL topology from view implementation
Supports nested namespaces, parameters, and reverse-resolution metadata
costs: Pattern ordering and nested resolver state affect behavior
Resolver population and URL configuration add indirection to a request path

features.name: Adaptive sync/async middleware chain
features.description: BaseHandler builds a middleware chain from settings.MIDDLEWARE, adapts sync and async handlers to the selected mode, and applies view, template-response, and exception middleware around the resolved view.
benefits: Cross-cutting concerns are configured independently of views
The same framework exposes synchronous and asynchronous request paths
costs: Ordering and mode adaptation can introduce context switches and lifecycle complexity
Middleware capability declarations must match implementation behavior

features.name: Model registry and ORM boundary
features.description: ModelBase constructs model classes and registers them with the application registry; Django's model layer exposes field and relation metadata that the query and database layers consume.
benefits: Domain models provide a declarative boundary for persistence and relations
The registry enables reverse relations and application-wide model lookup
costs: Metaclass and registry behavior add import and lifecycle coupling
ORM abstractions can hide database-specific costs and query behavior

features.name: Template response boundary
features.description: Django provides template loaders and engines and lets the handler apply template-response middleware after a view returns a response that may defer rendering.
benefits: Separates presentation templates from view and model code
Template loading and response processing are explicit extension boundaries
costs: Template lookup, context, escaping, and rendering add a second execution model
Deferred rendering changes when errors and resource work occur

mathematical_views.model: Configured application and model registry state machine
mathematical_views.question: How do installed applications transition from configuration to imported, model-ready, and ready states?
assumptions: Application configs and models are registry vertices with readiness state
Population phases and locks are abstract transitions
The view excludes all side effects of arbitrary application import code

mathematical_views.model: Recursive URL pattern tree with labeled leaves
mathematical_views.question: How does a URL path traverse nested patterns and produce a callback plus captured arguments?
assumptions: URLResolver and URLPattern objects form a rooted tree
Edges represent nested prefixes and leaves represent callbacks
The view abstracts regex/path compiler implementation and reverse lookup

mathematical_views.question: How do middleware wrappers, view processing, template-response processing, and exception handling surround a request?
assumptions: The middleware list is an ordered composition of state transformers
Request and response traversal directions may differ
Sync/async adapters preserve an intended callable interface but not necessarily identical cost

mathematical_views.question: How do model classes, fields, relations, application registration, and query operations form a persistence-facing graph?
assumptions: Models and fields are graph nodes and relation metadata are edges
The ORM view abstracts SQL compilation and backend-specific execution
It describes architectural boundaries and does not assert query equivalence or performance

benefits: Reusable app configuration and central readiness tracking
costs: Import order and global registry lifecycle become constraints

benefits: Explicit nested URL and callback separation
costs: Resolver indirection and ordering affect request behavior
Mode adaptation and order add runtime complexity
Metaclass/registry coupling and hidden database costs
Deferred rendering and template semantics add another lifecycle
